note: The reference-machine baseline for the shipped product. This is what closes PRD open question 7 ("confirm both after the first /bench run on the reference machine"), and it is the first bench run that measures the application rather than a harness: PRD 9.1.2's /bench route now flies the shipped scene — star field, camera rig, plane labels, thumbnail tier, focused card and its planets — over the production dataset, at the 87-plane roster. baseline-2026-09-04.json is superseded, not regressed against: it measured Phase 2a's harness (no card tier, no thumbnails, no labels, no rig) on a shorter six-segment path at 83 planes, so no segment in it has a counterpart here. `vsync` is the protocol run and the one PRD 7.2 is judged on; `uncapped` adds --disable-gpu-vsync to show the real headroom, because a 120 Hz panel reports 8.3 ms whether the frame cost 2 ms or 8.
verdict: PRD 7.2 target (60 fps, p95 <= 16.7 ms) MET and ceiling (50 fps, p95 <= 33 ms) MET, on both runs. Steady-state cost is 2.9 ms at p95 uncapped against a 16.7 ms target — about 5.7x headroom — so the ceilings in PRD 7.2 are confirmed as commitments this machine keeps comfortably, and the targets are met rather than merely approached. Open question 7 is answered: both rows stand as written.
caveats: Worst-frame times are not steady state, and they split into two different things. The vsync run's spikes (45.4 ms in `small-plane`, 31.8 ms in `sheet`) sit on focus boundaries, where a plane's shards are fetched and parsed (PRD 8.7.6) and the thumbnail atlas is uploaded; that is one frame in 4,606, and PRD 7.2's 33 ms ceiling is written against p95, which is 9.6 ms. The uncapped run's 373.8 ms frame in `sheet` is NOT the same thing and is not an atlas upload: it is DEC-645, first seen in Phase 2a's harness — which had no card tier, no atlas, no rig and no labels — and it has now reproduced on the shipped scene, a different path, a different dataset and a different segment. It appears only with --disable-gpu-vsync, at ~670 fps, and is characterised there as a probable measurement-mode artefact rather than something a user can experience. Both are logged rather than smoothed over, because p50 and p95 hide both and a percentile-only report would have said nothing.

CPU time per frame is reported by the star field (StarScene.onFrame), so it is a floor rather than the whole scene's cost: the card tier's per-frame work is not in it. Both runs report 0.0-0.1 ms against a 2 ms target, so the conclusion does not turn on the gap, but the figure should not be quoted as the complete render-loop cost.

GPU memory for thumbnails, planets and card images (PRD 7.2) is not in this file. It is measured through the ?probe=1 seam by scripts/verify-browser.mjs, which reports it against the 96 MB target and 160 MB ceiling.

PRD 7.3.4 ("no level-of-detail transition may pop") is not fully discharged by this file. The focus-boundary spikes above are the closest thing to a pop the bench can see, and they are one-frame events on a scripted teleport between focuses rather than on a real fly-to, which eases into the same transition over 1.2 s or more. Whether a transition pops for a user is judged in PRD 9.3's visual review, not here.
